learningObjectives: Identify major cortical, limbic and autonomic contributors to emotion regulation.
Differentiate reappraisal, attentional deployment, suppression and recovery.
Explain why arousal and context alter regulatory capacity.
Translate network mechanisms into practical clinical formulation.

anatomy.label: Amygdala
anatomy.detail: Rapidly evaluates emotionally salient cues and helps coordinate defensive responses.
anatomy.clinical: Hyperreactivity or poor contextual inhibition may amplify threat responding.

anatomy.label: Ventromedial prefrontal cortex
anatomy.detail: Integrates current goals, bodily value signals and contextual information.
anatomy.clinical: Reduced safety updating can prolong fear or avoidance.

anatomy.label: Lateral prefrontal cortex
anatomy.detail: Maintains alternative interpretations and task rules during reappraisal.
anatomy.clinical: Fatigue and stress can reduce access to deliberate strategies.

anatomy.label: Anterior insula
anatomy.detail: Maps interoceptive changes and subjective feeling intensity.
anatomy.clinical: Heightened interoceptive precision may intensify panic or distress.

anatomy.label: Hippocampus
anatomy.detail: Distinguishes present conditions from past associations.
anatomy.clinical: Context-generalised fear can make safe situations feel dangerous.

interaction.title: Explore Emotion Regulation Networks
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Detect
stages.text: Salience and limbic systems register a meaningful change.

stages.label: Contextualise
stages.text: Memory systems compare the present cue with past experience.

stages.label: Appraise
stages.text: The brain assigns meaning, value and predicted consequences.

stages.label: Regulate
stages.text: Attention, interpretation or action is adjusted to current goals.

stages.label: Recover
stages.text: Autonomic and behavioural systems return toward baseline.

quizBank.question: Which statement best describes emotion regulation?
options: Flexible shaping of emotional responses across time
quizBank.explanation: Regulation is a flexible, distributed process that changes attention, meaning, action and recovery.

quizBank.question: The hippocampus contributes to emotion regulation mainly by:
quizBank.explanation: Hippocampal context helps distinguish present safety from past threat associations.

quizBank.question: Why can severe arousal impair reappraisal?
options: Arousal constrains working memory and prefrontal control
The amygdala turns off all cognition
quizBank.explanation: High arousal can narrow attention and reduce access to deliberate control strategies.

quizBank.question: Suppression differs from reappraisal because suppression primarily:
options: Modifies outward response after emotion is underway
quizBank.explanation: Suppression targets expression, whereas reappraisal changes interpretation earlier in the process.

quizBank.question: The most useful clinical formulation asks:
options: Which regulatory operation is failing in which context?
Why is the client choosing to be emotional?
Which single brain region is broken?
How can all emotion be removed?
quizBank.explanation: Mechanism- and context-based formulation is more accurate than moral or single-region explanations.

reviewPrompts: Which statement best describes emotion regulation?
The hippocampus contributes to emotion regulation mainly by:
The goal is flexible, context-sensitive responding—not feeling less. A regulated nervous system can still produce intense emotion when the situation warrants it.
